Question: Which of the following is an example of a double-bind message

Options: 
A. A brother tells his sister, "You can use my car if you want to, but remember last time when you had an accident."
B. A coach tells a player, "You can try that move if you want, but remember it didn't work out last time."
C. A teacher tells a student, “You can do that if you want to, but I would appreciate it if you would not
D. A doctor tells a patient, "You can skip the medication if you want, but the pain might return."
E. A teacher tells a student, "You can skip the homework if you want, but your grades might drop."
F. A father tells his son, “I sure hope you can come to the movies with us tonight,” when his tone and posture thar he does not hope so

Definition of Double-Bind (Erich Fromm): A message sent to an individual, verbominally consistent, while behaving in a different way. Usually, there is a contradiction between words and non-verbal signals, or between a positive command and a negative context, leaving the recipient in an impossible situation where any response confirms the illegality or fault while satisfying doesn't. It often involves conflicting instructions: one says "X", the other says "not X", but the person believes must do X. Sometimes it's positive-negative paradox (congruent words, incongruent tone/body language).
